title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.834347: a pathwise waste bound on the 256-walk exact-accounting package

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel rho algorithm of proof.md/upstream-proof.md stops on every run within 2^125.834347 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Under disclosed H1, borrow premise C and 2-cycle premise P1, recovery probability is at least 0.39000001. Parameters: M=2^23, R=2^26, kappa=1.00008, w=2^-14.94, p0=0.39000012, Bennett tail t=2^70 with per-operation bound b=2^22. C bounds expected dx,dy,u borrows by (1/2+2^-10,1/2+2^-11,1/2+2^-11)E[L]; P1 bounds expected 2-cycles by E[L]/(4R). The kappa-rule waste is pathwise: 5.5's Ville lemma bounds 2-cycle catches by (1+2^-11)q'(S+2^61), so realised waste is (1+2^-11)*8,449/(4R)+16,158*2^-49.99999 < 2^-14.9547 < w outside one 2^-140 event, not only in expectation. Memory <2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Direct base: accepted c8a6819e (branch 9f06f2bf, 125.834417), whose credited packages are declared where materially reused. CORR=37798701/2^23 is charged per walk. The declared initial experiment and certificate ran separately (evidence.md); the ledger is recomputed in certificate.py. Analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Check production identities, a time-limited toy pipeline, interpreter execution of the shipped kernels and exits against reference arithmetic, counts, ledger and census rules. This is not a production-scale attack; evidence.md describes limitations.
